title: Sensory Analysis & Evaluation: Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch into descriptive panels, bias control and writing up results.
meta_desc: Stretch GCSE sensory analysis: descriptive panels, bias, presenting data, evaluation.
final_note: Honest evaluation is part of every great food product.

walkthroughs.body_html: A descriptive panel of trained tasters rates many attributes — sweetness, bitterness, crunch, glossiness — usually on 0-10 scales. Results map a product's sensory "fingerprint" and let designers tweak recipes precisely.

Bias comes from labels, expectations and tasting order. Counter it with sensory booths, coded samples, neutral lighting and random sample order to avoid order effect. Use unsalted crackers and water between samples to clear the palate.

A sensory report should state aim, method, sample, panel, results (charts) and conclusion. Compare results back to the brief: was the new low-sugar version still acceptable? Suggest one specific change for the next iteration.
